prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S231: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides readiness evidence showing that orbit products, maneuver screening, and conjunction coordination can be performed within the committed planning cycle.
S232: The Payload Processing Facility demonstrates that science product generation can be sustained during representative contact patterns without manual intervention beyond approved operator actions.
S233: The Network Control System records rehearsal outcomes for planned maintenance, station loss, degraded routing, and restoration of nominal connectivity after a simulated outage.
S234: The Ground Network Manager accepts the antenna readiness baseline only when the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna have current maintenance clearances.
S235: The Spacecraft Operations Team conducts at least one integrated day-in-the-life rehearsal that includes pass preparation, commanding discipline, telemetry surveillance, anomaly declaration, and recovery reporting.
S236: The Flight Dynamics Team conducts a separate rehearsal for missed tracking data and late orbit update availability to confirm that planning products remain usable under degraded conditions.
S237: The Payload Calibration Team validates that calibration operations are represented in the rehearsal schedule and that product quality decisions can be traced to approved engineering criteria.
S238: The Cybersecurity Desk participates in the final exercise by validating alert routing, privileged access review, and incident coordination with operations management.
S239: The User Services Portal uses the Product Hold List to prevent release of affected products until the applicable hold condition has been cleared.
S240: The Mission Planning System applies the delta note during schedule validation to ensure that contact and activity timing remains consistent with the latest operational constraint.
S241: The Backup Processing Cluster uses the Storage Watermark Snapshot to verify that recovery capacity is sufficient before it accepts routine standby responsibility.
S242: Osprey rejects any command request that lacks the approved authorization state, validation result, and operator acknowledgment required for routine service.
S243: Granite preserves the accepted archive baseline and confirms that retrieval tests meet the service objective before routine operations are declared stable.
S244: Operational key performance indicators include contact success rate, telemetry completeness, command validation timeliness, product latency, product quality disposition time, archive availability, help desk responsiveness, and unresolved anomaly age.
S245: Each key performance indicator has an assigned data source, sampling interval, review owner, threshold, and corrective action trigger so that routine reporting does not depend on informal judgment.
S246: The primary monthly service review compares actual performance against the accepted baseline and records trend explanations for any measure that moves outside the watch band.
S247: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are baselined with approved software versions, processing configurations, capacity reservations, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions before handover.
S248: Configuration baselines for ground software, operational procedures, interface control data, account roles, and monitoring rules are frozen at readiness review entry and changed only through approved change control.
S249: Handover to routine mission service is authorized when acceptance evidence is complete, rehearsals meet their objectives, open risks are acknowledged by accountable owners, and support teams confirm on-call coverage.
S250: After handover, the first operational reporting cycle is treated as a stabilization period in which deviations are reviewed daily and permanent process changes are deferred until sufficient evidence is available.
